To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the refined cluster function theory is an effective and powerful method to describe nuclear reactions and that the method has been applied to the description of reactions of light nuclei.
the refined cluster model is a general and powerful method to calculate the reaction cross sections for nuclear reactions.
the refined cluster model is an effective tool for the description of nuclear reactions and that it can also be used to calculate the properties of bound states.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problems: (a) the construction of a refined cluster model which is able to describe the reactions of light nuclei in a satisfactory manner, (b) the construction of an approximate theory of the nuclear shell model which is able, on the one hand, to reproduce the results of the refined cluster model and which, on the other hand, allows for the description of the reactions of heavy nuclei.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the refined cluster model is the most general method to describe reactions of nuclear systems.
a theory of nuclear reactions is given, which is based on a consistent and complete mathematical formalism.
the theory given is a very general and flexible tool which allows the calculation of the reaction matrix for any nuclear reaction in terms of a set of linear matrix equations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the theory of nuclear reactions is reduced to the solution of a set of coupled linear matrix equations.
a set of linear matrix equations is derived which is equivalent to the Schrödinger equation in the limit of large numbers of particles.
the refined cluster functions are the most general functions of cluster theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the refined cluster model can be applied to reactions of nuclei in the same way as to bound state problems.
we have shown that the refined cluster functions can be used in a very efficient way to describe reactions of bound and unbound nuclear states.
the cluster functions can be expressed in a form which is suitable to describe reactions of nuclear systems, i.e. as functions of the energy and the scattering angles of the particles.
